title: returning a value whose type has a foreign `Promise` constituent is an escape of executable foreign provenance
notes: poc/src/language/README.md, `SMITHERS1508`: 'executable foreign provenance escapes through an unsupported higher-order/return/store boundary.' This case carries NO `@throws` marker anywhere, which is its whole job: it is the control for a-trusted-union-with-a-promise-constituent-keeps-its-rejection-channel, and it localizes that case's extra SMITHERS1508 to the pre-existing union handling in `containsForeignExecutableValue` rather than to the trust rule. Two cases that diverge for one shared reason are worth more than one case that diverges for a reason nobody isolated.

xfail.reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 through `run.mjs --backend go --json --filter union`, and the marker's previous sentence was WRONG about the observation, not merely out of date. It said the fork reports [SMITHERS1301@5:23] alone. It does not: the fork reports a single stock TypeScript error, `TS2322@6:3` — "Type 'SmithersErr<Panic> | SmithersOk<string | Promise<string>>' is not assignable to the success type 'string' of 'Result<string, Panic>'" — and NO Smithers diagnostic at all. Confirmed against a pristine `git worktree` at HEAD as well as the working tree, so this is a stale note and not a regression. THAT CHANGES THE VERDICT, not just the wording. The fork does not omit SMITHERS1508 while otherwise agreeing; it never reaches its own foreign-boundary or must-use rules on this program, because its checker rejects the lowered return first. BOTH BACKENDS STILL REFUSE THE PROGRAM, so this is fail-closed and no checked failure escapes — but the fork refuses it for a reason that has nothing to do with foreign provenance, and a fork that later learned SMITHERS1508 would still not satisfy this case while the TS2322 stands in front of it. What must be fixed is therefore the ORDER as much as the rule: the union return has to reach the foreign-provenance walk before the assignability check refuses the lowered form. This case no longer retires in one edit with a-trusted-union-with-a-promise-constituent-keeps-its-rejection-channel, whose fork observation is [SMITHERS1502@5:23]; that earlier claim rested on the same mis-measurement. The two still share ONE cause — the union arm of `containsForeignExecutableValue` reports no SMITHERS1508 on either — and that is the only thing they share.
xfail.doc: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": the panic case is a property of calling an unannotated foreign runtime value, and a foreign `Promise` that leaves the function un-awaited carries that call out with it.
